diagrams.title: Systemic Associations of Oral Ulcers and Erosions
diagrams.subtitle: A mechanism-based differential for targeted history and testing

children.name: Complex aphthosis
children.detail: Near-continuous oral ± genital aphthae without sufficient Behçet features.

children.name: Behçet syndrome
children.detail: Genital ulcers/scars, ocular, vascular, neurologic, skin, GI disease.

children.name: IBD / celiac
children.detail: GI symptoms, perianal disease, malabsorption/nutrient deficiency.

children.name: SLE / connective tissue disease
children.detail: Photosensitivity, arthritis, renal/hematologic disease; oral discoid or palatal lesions.

children.name: Mucous membrane pemphigoid
children.detail: Scarring mucosal disease; linear BMZ immunoreactants.

children.name: Erosive lichen planus
children.detail: Reticular white striae with erosions/desquamative gingivitis.

children.name: Erythema multiforme / SJS-TEN
children.detail: Acute widespread erosions with skin/medication/infection context.

children.name: HSV
children.detail: Grouped vesicles/erosions, often keratinized mucosa in recurrence.

children.name: CMV / opportunistic
children.detail: Large chronic ulcers in immunocompromised host.

children.name: Medication injury
children.detail: Nicorandil, NSAIDs, chemotherapy, methotrexate toxicity, mTOR inhibitors and others.

children.name: Iron, B12, folate and other deficiency
children.detail: Test when diet, anemia, malabsorption, or severe recurrent disease suggests.

root.name: Recurrent oral ulceration / erosion
root.detail: Organize by mechanism and accompanying findings.

citations.quote: Review presents an etiologic classification and diagnostic algorithm for recurrent oral ulceration.
EULAR recommendations address mucocutaneous, ocular, vascular, neurologic, gastrointestinal, and joint involvement in Behçet syndrome.
European MMP guideline recommends direct immunofluorescence with serology and interdisciplinary management for mucosa-predominant disease.

diagrams.title: Oral Ulcer and Erosion Treatment by Cause
diagrams.subtitle: Do not escalate immunosuppression until infection, malignancy, and the mucosal diagnosis are sufficiently addressed

local.text: Topical corticosteroid started early; topical anesthetic, protective paste, bland rinses, trauma avoidance and correction of deficiency.

systemic.text: Frequent/severe disease: colchicine is a common first systemic option; short systemic glucocorticoid or other steroid-sparing therapy for selected refractory cases.

organ-risk.text: Reopen the diagnosis for major, scarring, near-continuous, late-onset, or systemically symptomatic disease.

local.text: Topical corticosteroid and analgesic care for individual ulcers.

systemic.text: Colchicine or apremilast are common options for recurrent oral/genital ulcers; azathioprine, TNF inhibitor, interferon or other therapy depends on full phenotype.

organ-risk.text: Uveitis/retinal vasculitis, vascular, neurologic or severe GI disease requires urgent organ-specific immunosuppression and specialty care.

local.text: Potent topical corticosteroid and meticulous oral care can supplement systemic therapy.

systemic.text: Rituximab-based glucocorticoid-sparing therapy is standard for many moderate–severe patients; regimen and infection prevention require specialist management.

organ-risk.text: Severe pain, weight loss, dehydration, widespread skin disease or infection may require hospital-level care.

local.text: High-potency topical corticosteroid for limited oral disease; dental hygiene and candidiasis prevention.

systemic.text: Dapsone or systemic immunosuppression/biologic therapy according to severity and antigen/phenotype.

organ-risk.text: Ocular, laryngeal, esophageal or genital disease can scar irreversibly; urgent multidisciplinary treatment.

local.text: Support hydration, pain control and oral hygiene; manage secondary candidiasis when present.

systemic.text: Pathogen-directed antiviral, antibacterial or antifungal therapy based on clinical testing.

organ-risk.text: Fever/neutropenia, disseminated infection, inability to swallow or an immunocompromised host may require admission.

citations.quote: Review summarizes diagnosis and stepwise treatment of recurrent aphthous stomatitis.
EULAR recommendations address mucocutaneous, ocular, vascular, neurologic, gastrointestinal, and joint involvement in Behçet syndrome.
European MMP guideline recommends direct immunofluorescence with serology and interdisciplinary management for mucosa-predominant disease.
